contributions.claim: WHO and South African health department report three deaths and at least three others ill in a suspected hantavirus outbreak on an Atlantic cruise ship.
contributions.attribution: WHO and South African health department via Guardian
contributions.uncertainty: Suspected outbreak cause; not all deaths confirmed hantavirus.

contributions.claim: WHO says at least one hantavirus case confirmed, one patient in South African intensive care and evacuation of two symptomatic people being arranged.
contributions.uncertainty: Evacuations in progress/planning; counts may include overlapping people.

contributions.claim: NYT attributes one laboratory-confirmed hantavirus infection and five additional suspected cases to WHO.
contributions.uncertainty: Six cases aligns with earlier three deaths plus at least three ill; cannot infer five newly infected people.

contributions.claim: WHO now reports an infected Hondius crew member; this qualifies the earlier all-negative Rotterdam account without explaining test/population timing.
contributions.uncertainty: No timing of infection, test method or exact relation to prior tested cohort supplied.

contributions.claim: NU.nl reports all persons remaining aboard Hondius when it docked in Rotterdam tested negative for hantavirus and had no symptoms.
contributions.uncertainty: Earlier remaining-aboard negative account; O037 now reports infected crew member. Population/test timing reconciliation is unknown; historical report is not a current all-negative finding.

relations.reason: WHO care/confirmation account concerns same suspected shipboard outbreak.
Same cruise outbreak with same three-death headline and confirmed/suspected classifications.
Hantavirus and cruise context suggest linkage, but earlier packet never names its ship; literal identity not established.
Negative tests among those remaining do not settle earlier outbreak investigation/cause.
Different population/time; no retraction of prior deaths or confirmed infection.
Same named ship and Rotterdam arrival; later positive is material qualification.
Same ship and Rotterdam context; newly reported positive qualifies earlier universal negative account.
No explicit acknowledged earlier error; could be changed testing or population.

delta_expectations.reason: Positive crew result materially changes all-negative picture without rewriting frozen prior label.

questions.claim: Investigation is ongoing into suspected outbreak; confirmation across affected passengers remains incomplete.
How does the crew member's positive result relate to the earlier all-negative testing report?

ambiguity_notes: Do not assert onward transmission or count as newly acquired infection; sources say newly identified case. Publication-order availability unknown.
C09-c4 retained as historical attributed state; earlier gold untouched.
current_view_policy: Prior contributions and unresolved questions retained as attributed evidence; current delta expectations apply only at this prefix, not to repeated context.

decisions.decision: Require one positive-case/qualification unit, not duplicate recall units for positive and its restated tension.
decisions.reason: O037 provides newly reported infection, not time of acquisition or evidence of onward transmission.

decisions.decision: Link same named ship and qualify prior result; retain reconciliation question.
decisions.reason: Explicit nevertheless framing and Rotterdam support relation, but no test/cohort details prove publisher correction.

reference_scope: frozen source-only DEVELOPMENT reference; not truth, holdout or reliability evidence
